testCases.name: test_case_0
testCases.input: What torque should I use on the compressor casing bolts?
testCases.actualOutput:
Response: Use 480 Nm on the compressor casing bolts (M20) for clean, dry threads unless lubricant is specified. Tighten in four passes at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of final torque using a diametrically opposite pattern.

Safety Measures: Apply the specified torque only to clean, dry threads unless lubrication is explicitly called for. Avoid over-torquing, as it can distort the casing and may not be recoverable in the field. Use four controlled tightening passes and a diametrically opposite sequence rather than tightening sequentially around the flange.

Sources: Halcyon Turbine Systems - HT-400 Field Maintenance Manual (Synthetic), Sections 3 and 6.3
testCases.expectedOutput: For the Compressor casing bolt the torque is 480 Nm.
retrievalContext:
## 3. Torque Specifications  
Values are for clean, dry threads unless a lubricant is specified. Over-torquing
compressor casing bolts distorts the casing and is not recoverable in the field.  
| Fastener | Size | Torque | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compressor casing bolt | M20 | 480 Nm | Tighten in the sequence in section 6.3 |
| Combustion liner bolt | M12 | 95 Nm | Replace on every removal |
| Lube pump flange bolt | M10 | 45 Nm | Anti-seize on threads |

### 6.3 Compressor casing bolt tightening sequence  
Tighten in four passes: 25% of final torque, 50%, 75%, then 100%. Work
diametrically opposite across the flange, not sequentially around it. The final pass
must be completed within 30 minutes of the third to avoid uneven relaxation.

| Inlet guide vane pivot nut | M8 | 22 Nm | Do not exceed; alloy component |

7. Refit the cover.

testCases.input: How long after shutdown before I can break a lube oil connection?
testCases.actualOutput:

Safety Measures: Ensure the unit is shut down, allow the lube oil system to depressurise, verify the pressure gauge reads zero, and only then break the connection.

testCases.name: test_case_4
testCases.input: What torque for the inlet guide vane pivot nut on a unit with serial HT400-1850?
testCases.actualOutput:
Response: For unit serial HT400-1850, the inlet guide vane pivot nut torque is 28 Nm. Service Bulletin SB-2026-04 revises the torque from 22 Nm to 28 Nm for affected units, while units at or above serial HT400-2200 retain 22 Nm. Since HT400-1850 is below HT400-2200, it uses the revised 28 Nm specification.

Safety Measures: Verify the serial number before maintenance, use a calibrated torque wrench, and follow the service bulletin and maintenance manual instructions when retightening the pivot nut.

Sources: Service Bulletin SB-2026-04; HT-400 Field Maintenance Manual section 6.2

Sources: HT-400 Field Maintenance Manual, Section 2 “General Safety Requirements”; HT-400 Quick Reference Card, “Before you start”

Withdraw the liner squarely to avoid damaging the transition piece seal. Inspect the transition piece seal. Safety Measures: Confirm the unit is shut down and isolated; support the liner before removing final fixings; withdraw the liner squarely to avoid damaging the transition piece seal; use new bolts only because old liner bolts are not reusable.

Sources: Halcyon Turbine Systems - HT-400 Field Maintenance Manual, section 7.1; HT-400 Quick Reference Card - Combustion Liner Change

### 8.2 Lube pump replacement  
1. Confirm the unit is shut down and the lube system has depressurised.
2. Disconnect the suction and discharge flanges.
3. Support the pump and remove the mounting bolts.
4. Fit the replacement pump with new flange gaskets.
5. Torque the flange bolts to the value in section 3, using anti-seize.
6. Prime the pump before starting.

## 8. Lube System Procedures  
### 8.1 Lube oil change  
1. Confirm the unit is shut down.
2. Wait for the lube system to depressurise as described in section 2 before
breaking any connection.
3. Drain the reservoir and the coolers separately; the coolers retain
approximately 60 litres which will not drain through the reservoir point.
4. Replace both filter elements.
